text:
11.  
Josep has 4 toys: a car, a doll, a ball, and a boat. He wants to place them side by side on a shelf. In how many ways can he arrange the 4 toys if he wants both the boat and the doll to be next to the car?
label: B

text: 13. For 3 days, the cat Joy has been catching mice. Each day, he caught 2 more mice than the day before. On the third day, he caught twice as many mice as he had caught on the first day. In total, how many mice did Joy catch over the three days?
label: C

text: The date of next May 5th, written as 5/5/2015, is the first from today that contains three fives. What will be the next date that also contains three fives?
label: E

text:
5.  
Marc has 9 candies and Tomàs has 17. How many candies does Tomàs need to give to Marc so that they both have the same amount?
label: C

text:
9.  
Ricard and Tomàs are building an igloo. Every hour, Ricard makes 8 snow blocks, and Tomàs makes two blocks fewer. How many blocks can they make together in 3 hours?
label: C

text: 15. Time passes differently on planet Iris compared to Earth. One hour on Earth is equivalent to three days on planet Iris. The months on planet Iris have 5 weeks, and each week has 6 days. How many Earth hours are equivalent to 2 months of the calendar on planet Iris?
label: C

text: 19. The combination to open a safe is a number with four different digits. How many combinations are there if only 1, 3, 5, and 7 can be used?
label: C

text: 2. Some pirates climb up a rope, one after the other, to attack a ship. The captain is in the middle of all of them, the eighth whether counting from the beginning or from the end. How many pirates are on the rope?
label: D

text: 6. Alicia has placed 6 triangular tiles in a line. Then, between every two triangular tiles, she has placed a square tile. Finally, between each square tile and each triangular tile, she has placed a round tile. How many round tiles has she placed in total?
label: D

text: 10. Berta and Guillem are standing in line to enter the theater. Berta knows there are 7 people in front of her. Guillem knows there are 11 people in total in the line. If Berta is directly in front of Guillem, how many people are behind Guillem?
label: A

text: 15. The Kangaroo makes 10 jumps in one minute and rests for the next 3 minutes, then makes another 10 jumps in one minute and rests for another 3 minutes, and so on. How many minutes will have passed when the Kangaroo has made 50 jumps?
label: D

text: 12. We have four cards, each with one of the digits 2, 0, 1, and 8. How many different two-digit numbers can we make with them that are greater than 10 and less than 25?
label: A

text: 13. Alicia has 3 sheets of white paper, 2 black ones, and 2 gray ones. First, she cuts the sheets that are not black in half. Then, she cuts the sheets that are not white in half. How many pieces of paper will she have in the end?
label: D

text: 1. Mother Kangaroo and her daughter Little Kangaroo weigh 60 kg together. On her own, the mother weighs 52 kg. How much does Little Kangaroo weigh?
label: B

text: 19. In a zoo, there are 10 animals from the camelid family. They have camels (with two humps) and dromedaries (with one hump). In total, we count 14 humps. How many camels are there in the zoo?
label: D

text: 5. There are 12 children waiting in line at the zoo entrance. Llum is the seventh in line from the front, and Quim is the second from the end. How many children are there between Llum and Quim?
label: B

text: 13. In a basket, there are some red apples and 8 pears. The pears can be either green or yellow. There are 6 yellow pears, and there are 3 more apples than pieces of green fruit. How many apples are in the basket?
label: B

text: 22. At the Kangaroo summer camp, a total of 43 people attended, and they were grouped into teams of 5 or 6 members. How many teams were there at the Kangaroo camp?
label: B

text: 24. Joan and Ada exchanged sweets. At first, Joan gave Ada as many sweets as Ada had. Then, Ada gave Joan as many sweets as Joan had after the first exchange. After these two exchanges, each of them had 4 sweets. How many sweets did Joan have at the beginning?
label: B

text: 16. In a tennis tournament, the Almosta team, which has three players, competes against the Petricó team, which has two players. Each match is played between one member of one team and one member of the other team, and all possible different matches are played. How many matches will be played?
label: B

text: 19. The kangaroo had two branches for lunch. Each branch had 10 leaves. The kangaroo ate some leaves from the first branch. Then, from the second branch, it ate as many leaves as it had left on the first branch. How many uneaten leaves were left in total on both branches?
label: D

text:
24. Jordi has a box with balls. He also has balls outside the box. Each turn, he does the following:  
he removes half of the balls from the box, puts two balls inside, and adds to the box as many balls as it currently contains. He has done this 35 times, and the box finally contains 148 balls. How many balls were there at the beginning?
label: A

text: 11. Three zebras, Runa, Zara, and Biba, are participating in a contest where the zebra with the most stripes wins. Runa has 15 stripes, Zara has 3 more than Runa, and Runa has 5 fewer stripes than Biba. How many stripes does the winning zebra have?
label: C

text: 20. Isabel has a box with 3 chocolates of one kind, 4 of another, and 6 of a third type. How many chocolates does she need to take out of the box, without looking, to ensure she has chosen one of each type?
label: D

text:
20. Three frogs live in a pond. Every night, one of the frogs sings a song to the other two.  
After 9 nights, we know that the first frog has sung 2 times and that the second frog has heard 5 songs.  
How many songs has the third frog heard?
label: B

text: 3. A number has three digits that, when multiplied, give 15. What is the sum of the three digits of this number?
label: B

text: 8. Llúís has 7 apples and 2 bananas. Llúís gives 2 apples to Jordi, and Jordi gives bananas to Llúís. Then Llúís has as many apples as bananas. How many bananas did Jordi give to Llúís?
label: B

text: 17. The sum of two numbers is 170. The larger number ends in 5. If we remove this 5, we obtain the other number. What is the difference between these two numbers?
label: D

text: 6. The combination to open a safe is a three-digit number with different digits. How many combinations are there if only 1, 3, and 5 can be used?
label: E

text: 7. In a bag, there are 10 red socks, 8 blue socks, and 11 black socks. What is the minimum number of socks we need to take out, in the dark, to be sure we have taken out a pair of the same color?
label: A

text: 11. In a small zoo, there is a giraffe, an elephant, a lion, and a turtle. Maria wants to plan a route to visit two different animals. She does not want to start with the lion. How many different routes can she take?
label: D

text: 16. Four siblings have eaten 11 pastries in total. Each of them has eaten at least one pastry. All of them have eaten a different number of pastries. Three of them have eaten a total of 9 pastries, and one of the siblings has eaten exactly 3. How many pastries has the sibling who ate the most eaten?
label: A

text: 7. In a store, balloons are sold in packs of 5 balloons, 10 balloons, or 25 balloons. Mateu wants to buy 70 balloons. What is the smallest number of packs needed to provide him with the 70 balloons?
label: B

text: 9. Jaume wants to cook 5 dishes in a kitchen that only has two burners. To cook one of the five dishes, he needs 40 minutes; for another, 15 minutes; for another, 35 minutes; for another, 10 minutes; and for the remaining one, 45 minutes. He can cook them in whatever order works best for him using the two burners, and each dish must remain on the same burner for the entire indicated time without being removed before it is fully cooked. What is the minimum time required to prepare all five dishes?
label: C

text: 9. There are butterflies and dragonflies on the flowers of a rose bush. The rose bush has 8 flowers, and there is no more than one insect on each flower, but more than half of the flowers have insects. If the number of butterflies is double the number of dragonflies, how many butterflies are there?
label: C

text: 12. On a farm, there are 15 animals, including cows, chickens, and goats. We know that exactly 10 animals are not cows and that exactly 8 are not chickens. How many cows and chickens are there in total?
label: D

text: 21. The pages of a book are numbered 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, ... and so on. Among all the digits used to number the pages, the digit 5 appears exactly 16 times. What is the maximum number of pages the book can have?
label: C

text: Grandma Helena and Grandpa Josep went mushroom hunting and picked 18. Grandma found 2 more than Grandpa. How many mushrooms did Grandpa find?
label: D

text: 12. The sum of three numbers is 50. Cinta subtracts a secret number from each of the three numbers and obtains 24, 13, and 7. Which of the following numbers is one of the three original numbers?
label: A

text: 18. The kangaroo has to guess a 3-digit number that the little kangaroo has thought of. The kangaroo says these three numbers: 123, 145, 643. The little kangaroo replies that each time, only one digit is correct and in its correct position. What is the number the little kangaroo has thought of?
label: D

text: 16. The kangaroo had, for lunch, three branches with 20 leaves each. It ate some leaves from the first branch. Then, from the second branch, it ate as many leaves as were left on the first branch. Finally, from the third branch, it ate two leaves. How many uneaten leaves were left across the three branches?
label: E

text: 21. A box contains fewer than 50 cookies. These cookies can be evenly distributed among 2, 3, or 4 children. However, 6 more cookies would be needed to distribute them evenly among 7 children. How many cookies are in the box?
label: D

text:
8. At the kiosk, they sell all the comics at the same price, and at the start of the day, they already had money in the cash register.  
After selling 6 comics, they have €70 in the cash register. By the end of the day, they have sold a total of 16 comics, and there is €120 in the cash register. How much money was in the cash register initially?
label: C

text: 11. The students in a class are seated in rows. There is the same number of students in each row. There are 2 rows of students in front of Robert, 1 row of students behind him, 3 students to his left, and 5 students to his right. How many students are there in this class?
label: E

text:
13. Three football teams participate in a tournament. Each team plays only once against the other two.  
In each match, the winner earns 3 points, and the loser earns none. In the case of a draw, each team earns 1 point.  
After all the matches, what number of points can no team have obtained?
label: D

text: 11. Jasmina has to transport 20 books from an encyclopedia from her classroom to the school library, which is 40 meters away. She can only carry 3 books per trip. How many meters will she travel to transport all the books?
label: B

text: 16. The four-digit number 2024 has three special properties: all the digits are even numbers; it has three different digits, one of which is repeated, and the last digit is equal to the sum of the first three. How many four-digit numbers (including 2024) have these three properties?
label: D

text: 23. Jordin has a certain number of candies and wants to distribute them among her nets, so that each one has a bag with the same number of candies. After putting in each bag the maximum possible number of candies, she sees that there are 8 in each bag and that there are 5 left over. What is the minimum number of candies she can have?
label: B

text: 13. In the country of Kangaroos, every June the population doubles, and every December one gets upset with the others and leaves. Today, in the country of Kangaroos, there are exactly three kangaroos. How many will there be on March 15, 2018?
label: B

text:
16. In a class, each of the boys has shaken hands with each of the girls.  
If a total of 77 handshakes have been made, how many students are there in this class?
label: B

text: 19. The sum of two natural numbers is 170. We know that one of the numbers ends in 5, and when this digit is removed, we obtain the second number. What is the difference between these two numbers?
label: C

text: 23. On the screen of a digital clock, two digits are displayed for the hour and two digits for the minutes; for example, 00:32 or 21:34. The four digits from the latter example appear at other times of the day in different positions: 21:43, 23:41, etc. How many times throughout the day do the digits 0, 1, 2, and 6 appear together?
label: A

text: 25. Joan was born on the same day his mother turned 20. Therefore, they always shared a birthday celebration. Both lived long lives. On how many birthdays was the mother's age a multiple of Joan's age?
label: C

text:
28. In an election, four candidates have run, and 2,000 valid votes have been counted.  
The winner received 100 votes more than the second; the second received 100 more than the third, and the third received 100 more than the fourth. How many votes did the winner receive?
label: E

text: 3. Anna has painted the squares located on the diagonals of a grid. What are the dimensions of this grid if she has painted a total of nine squares?
label: C

text: 2. Robert has written the following list of numbers on the board: 4, 5, 1, 5, 2, 3, 5, 4, 5, 5, 2, 3, 3, 1, 5, 4, 2. Call "coherent" those numbers that match the number of times they appear in the list. What is the sum of all the coherent numbers in this list, counting them every time they appear?
label: B

text: 21. How many times do the hands of a clock form a 90° angle between 8 a.m. and 12 noon?
label: D

text: 22. We have a special cubic die. Five faces are marked with the numbers 5, 6, 9, 11, and 14. Additionally, we know that the sum of the opposite faces of the die is the same. What is the number on the sixth face?
label: A

text: 23. We weigh a container that holds water up to one-third of its capacity, and the scale shows 600 g. Then we weigh it with water up to two-thirds of its capacity, and the scale shows 800 g. How much does the empty container weigh?
label: D

text: 25. Pere went hiking in the mountains for 5 days. He started on Monday, and the last stage was on Friday. Each day, he walked 2 km more than the previous day. When he completed the entire route, the total distance he had covered was 70 km. How many kilometers did Pere walk on Thursday?
label: A

text: 27. Consider the integer 1234567891011..............99100 that results from writing consecutively and in order all the integers from 1 to 100, one after the other. From this number, we erase all the digits equal to 1. How many digits remain written?
label: C

text: 9. A printer is not working properly. When a new job starts, it makes 14 consecutive copies correctly, and the next one comes out defective; that is, the 15th, the 30th, the 45th, etc., are defective. Joan has requested 2,500 copies without knowing about the problem. How many copies will he be able to use?
label: D

text: 23. A, B, and C are three different digits. We form 6-digit numbers using three A's, two B's, and one C. The largest number that can be obtained in this way can never be equal to
label: C

text: 24. The sum of the ages of Clàudia and her mother is 36, and the sum of the ages of her mother and her grandmother is 81. What was the grandmother's age when Clàudia was born?
label: B

text: 8. How many times do we need to roll a die with faces numbered from 1 to 6 to be certain that we will get a number that has already appeared before?
label: D

text: Ali Baba and the 40 thieves have divided 42 identical bags of gold coins among themselves. Each of them receives exactly the same share of the loot: one bag and, in addition, 2 coins. How many coins are there in each bag?
label: C

text:
12. We write the first six odd numbers, one on each face of a die that was blank.  
Toni rolls the die three times and adds up the results. Which of the following results cannot be the sum?
label: E

text: 13. Normally, the Cookie Monster eats a pack of 5 cookies every day. However, if the Monster is very hungry, on that day he eats two full packs. If the Monster has eaten 60 cookies over 9 days, how many days has he been very hungry?
label: E

text: 14. Ernest has square pieces, all of the same size, some white and others black. With all of them, he has constructed a larger square in such a way that all the pieces on the edges are black, and the others are white. If he has used 24 black pieces, how many white pieces has he used?
label: E

text: 17. In a daycare center, there are 14 girls and 12 boys. If half of the children go out to the playground, what is the minimum number of them that we can be sure are girls?
label: D

text:
19. A group of Kangaroo enthusiasts calls their mascot "rugnac" a curious animal they have designed. A friend arrives and asks them:

How many legs do six kittens and seven rugnacs have in total? She gets the answers 44, 51, 64, 76, and 80, because she knows that four of them told her a lie and one told the truth. How many legs does a rugnac have?
label: C

text: 24. We have built a metal structure. It consists of two cubes of different sizes, placed one inside the other, with the edges made of wire. Additionally, each vertex of one cube is connected to a vertex of the other cube, also with wire. How many wires make up this structure?
label: C

text: 23. We say that a three-digit number is beautiful if the middle digit is greater than the sum of the other two digits. What is the largest number of consecutive beautiful numbers that we can find?
label: C

text: 28. In a chess tournament, Magnus has to play 15 games. At a certain point, of the games he has played, he has won half, lost a third, and 2 have ended in a draw. How many games does Magnus still have left to play?
label: A

text: Miquel wants to prepare 24 muffins for his birthday party. To bake six muffins, two eggs are needed. Eggs are sold in boxes of 6. How many boxes does Miquel need to buy, at a minimum?
label: A

text: 8. Four baskets contain 1, 4, 6, and 9 apples, respectively. What is the minimum number of apples that need to be moved between baskets so that each basket has the same number of apples?
label: D

text:
27. We asked three pirates how many coins and diamonds their friend Barbaroja has. Each of them told the truth about one thing and lied about the other. Their answers were as follows:  
Pirate 1: 8 coins and 6 diamonds; Pirate 2: 7 coins and 4 diamonds; Pirate 3: 7 coins and 7 diamonds.  
What is the sum of the number of coins and diamonds that Barbaroja has?
label: C

text: 29. We have a cube with an edge length of 7 cm. On each of the six faces of this cube, we draw, in red, the two diagonals. Then, we cut the cube into small cubes, each with an edge length of 1 cm. How many of these small cubes have red paint on at least one of their faces?
label: E

text: 30. Ten characters have been found, each of them holding a card with a number from 1 to 10. Each card has a different number. Among the characters, some are trolls, who always lie, and the rest are elves, who always tell the truth. A visitor asked each of the characters what number was on their card; all of them responded with a number from 1 to 10, and the sum of the numbers they mentioned was 36. What is the minimum number of trolls that we can be certain are present at the gathering?
label: D

text: 10. In a pastry shop, chocolates are sold in three types of boxes: 5, 10, and 25 units. Toni wants to buy exactly 95 chocolates. What is the minimum number of boxes he needs to buy to achieve this?
label: B

text: 13. The year 2022 is a special year because the digit 2 appears three times. This is the third time that the turtle Eva has lived in a year with three identical digits. How old will Eva be, at least, by the end of the year 2022?
label: D

text:
14. Lisa has four dogs. Each of them weighs an integer number of kilograms, and no two of them weigh the same.  
The total weight of the four is 60 kg. Ordered by increasing weight, the third one weighs 28 kg. How much does the second one weigh?
label: A

text: 30. A group of 30 people are sitting around a round table. Some of them are wearing hats. Those who are not wearing hats must tell the truth, and those who are wearing hats can either tell the truth or lie. All of the people say: "At least one of my two neighbors is wearing a hat." What is the minimum number of people among the 30 that we can be certain, without looking, are wearing hats?
label: B

text: 5. Bruna has seven tiles, each with one of the following numbers: 4, 69, 9, 51, 113, 5, and 67. She forms twelve-digit numbers by placing the tiles side by side. If she has created the smallest possible twelve-digit number, what are the last three digits of this number?
label: A

text: 12. Five friends try to guess how many kangaroos are in a zoo, and they have said the following numbers: 2, 4, 5, 8, and 9. The kangaroo keeper at the park tells them: One of you has guessed four too many, and another has guessed two too few. How many kangaroos are there in the park?
label: B

text: 23. Martí has three cards with a number on each side. The first card has 1 on one side and 4 on the other; the second card has 2 and 5; and the third card has 3 and 6. Martí shuffles and flips the cards randomly, places them on the table, and adds up the three numbers that are visible. How many different sums can he obtain?
label: D

text: 27. A grandmother has a certain number of candies and wants to distribute them among her children, so that each one has a bag with the same number of candies. After putting in each bag the maximum possible number of candies, she sees that there are 20 in each bag and that she has 12 left. What is the minimum number of candies she can have?
label: C
